props.text: Most youth bikes arrive about 85% built. You fit the handlebars, front wheel, pedals and saddle, then set up the brakes. Tap each step as you finish it.
Cut the zip ties, remove the packaging and lay the parts out: front wheel, pedals marked L and R, saddle and reflectors.
Seat the stem, line the bars up with the front wheel and tighten the bolts evenly, a little at a time.
Seat the axle fully in the fork, then close the quick release or tighten both axle nuts. Spin it: it should run straight.
The right pedal threads clockwise, the left anticlockwise. Start both by hand, then snug them with the 15 mm wrench.
Insert the seat post at least to its minimum insertion mark, set the height below and tighten the clamp.
Hook the cable noodle into the V-brake arms and center the pads on the rim, not the tire. The wheel should lock before the lever reaches the grip.
Pump to the pressure printed on the sidewall and check the bead sits evenly all round.
Check every bolt, fit the reflectors and the bell, and test the brakes at walking pace.
Front wheel seated in the fork
Brake pads meet the rim squarely
Never above the minimum insertion mark
Start with the top of the saddle about **54 cm** from the ground so both feet touch flat. Once your child rides confidently, raise it to about **59 cm**, where only the balls of the feet touch.
Before the first ride: the brakes stop the bike, both wheels are tight, the bars do not twist against the front wheel and the helmet fits snugly.
